title: Lift a high ideal product into an ideal-power tensor product
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $I$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and $H$ a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every $n\geq0$ there exist $m\geq0$ and a morphism $a:I^{n+m}H\to I^n\otimes H$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] such that multiplication $\mu_n:I^n\otimes H\to H$ after $a$ equals the inclusion $I^{n+m}H\hookrightarrow H$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. All powers are ideal-sheaf-data powers and products are multiplication images. This statement has no open subset, target module, or local map.

source.place: Tag 01YB (coherent-lemma-homs-over-open), kernel of tensor multiplication and the second Artin-Rees argument, using Tag 01YA.

proof.text: Use coherence of H to obtain quasi-coherence. Apply the tensor kernel-control theorem to obtain coherence of T, quasi-coherence of K, and vanishing of I^n K.

The fixed-power Artin-Rees intersection bound supplies m. If z in I^m T maps to zero, its inclusion lies both in I^m T and in K, so it lies in the range of I^n K -> T, which is zero. Injectivity of the product inclusion gives z=0. Applying this to differences proves injectivity on every open, and hence monicity of restricted multiplication.

Identify the image of the restricted multiplication with I^(n+m)H. Since the restricted multiplication is monic, Mathlib imageMonoIsoSource identifies its image with I^m T. Compose the comparison with this canonical isomorphism and the inclusion into T; imageMonoIsoSource_hom_self gives the required multiplication identity.

theorem ideal_power_tensor_image_lift
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (H : X.Modules)
    (hH : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace H) (n : ℕ) :
    letI : MonoidalCategory X.Modules := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory X.sheaf
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (a : idealModuleProduct (I ^ (n + m)).toModulesι H ⟶
        (I ^ n).toModules ⊗ H),
      a ≫ ((I ^ n).toModulesι ▷ H ≫ (λ_ H).hom) =
        idealModuleProductι (I ^ (n + m)).toModulesι H
